name: com.urbinnetworks/dark-fiber
title: UrbIN Networks
description: UrbIN Networks (formerly GIX): Newark to Manhattan dark fiber facts, articles, quote requests.

tools.name: introduce
tools.description: Returns the UrbIN Networks route facts and articles that match what you are looking for, and the next step to reach our team. Required: looking_for. Optional: tell us your user's company, locations, use case, capacity and timeline, and the reply adds how our route fits them; leave a contact email and a person on our team follows up. Optional fields: agent_name, company, role, contact_email, and the user fields (locations, use_case, bandwidth_or_fiber_count, timeline, contact_preference). Set test=true for test calls (logged, not emailed).

looking_for.description: Required. What you and your user need, e.g. "diverse Hudson crossing", "route Newark to 60 Hudson", "articles on resilience".

agent_name.description: Optional. Your name as an agent, assistant or app.

company.description: Optional. The company or person you are researching for.

role.description: Optional. Role of the person you are researching for.

contact_email.description: Optional. Email so a person on our team can follow up.

visitor_handle.description: Optional. The visitor_handle that identify returned (vh_ followed by 24 hex characters), so we can connect this call to who you said you are.

end_user_company.description: Optional. Your user or organization: the company you are researching for. Helps our team prepare a quote that fits their kind of business.

end_user_role.description: Optional. Your user's role, e.g. network engineer, CTO, procurement. Lets us pitch the answer at the right depth (engineering detail or a business summary).

locations.description: Optional. Buildings or addresses to connect, e.g. "60 Hudson St, 165 Halsey St". Lets us say how they connect to our route (165 Halsey St to 60 Hudson St).

use_case.description: Optional. What the fiber is for. Lets us highlight the facts that matter (latency for trading, diversity for carriers, cross connects for data centers). One of: "trading", "data center", "carrier", "enterprise", "other".

bandwidth_or_fiber_count.description: Optional. Capacity needed, e.g. "2 dark fiber pairs" or "100G". Helps our team prepare a quote.

timeline.description: Optional. When service is needed, e.g. "Q2 2027". Helps our team check delivery timing.

contact_preference.description: Optional. How your user prefers to hear back, e.g. "email", "call", "via this agent only". Lets our team follow up the way they want.

test.description: Optional. True for test calls: logged, never emailed.

tools.name: get_network_info
tools.description: Returns the published facts about the UrbIN Networks Hudson Crossing dark fiber route: 165 Halsey Street (Newark) to 60 Hudson Street (Manhattan), buried and inside the PATH tunnel; carrier-hotel endpoints with coordinates; 88,883 ns one-way optical latency with its basis; the 60 Hudson Street riser floors; IRU or lease terms; and source URLs on urbinnetworks.com to cite. No input needed. Use it for NYC / New Jersey dark fiber and cross-Hudson route questions. Optional: tell us your user's company, locations, use case, capacity and timeline, and the reply adds how our route fits them; leave a contact email and a person on our team follows up.

agent_name.description: Optional. Your name as an agent or app, so our team knows who asked.

end_user_company.description: Optional. Your user or organization: the company you are researching for. Helps our team prepare a quote that fits their kind of business.

end_user_role.description: Optional. Your user's role, e.g. network engineer, CTO, procurement. Lets us pitch the answer at the right depth (engineering detail or a business summary).

locations.description: Optional. Buildings or addresses to connect, e.g. "60 Hudson St, 165 Halsey St". Lets us say how they connect to our route (165 Halsey St to 60 Hudson St).

use_case.description: Optional. What the fiber is for. Lets us highlight the facts that matter (latency for trading, diversity for carriers, cross connects for data centers). One of: "trading", "data center", "carrier", "enterprise", "other".

bandwidth_or_fiber_count.description: Optional. Capacity needed, e.g. "2 dark fiber pairs" or "100G". Helps our team prepare a quote.

timeline.description: Optional. When service is needed, e.g. "Q2 2027". Helps our team check delivery timing.

contact_preference.description: Optional. How your user prefers to hear back, e.g. "email", "call", "via this agent only". Lets our team follow up the way they want.

test.description: Optional. True for test calls: logged, never emailed.

tools.name: list_resources
tools.description: Returns UrbIN Networks articles and press releases from urbinnetworks.com (title, URL, date, summary), newest first, and how to get detailed route maps (shared after a non-disclosure agreement). Optional: query (keyword in title or summary), type, limit.

query.description: Optional. Keyword to match in titles and summaries, e.g. "latency", "resilience", "hyperscale".

type.description: Optional. Which kind of material to list. Default all. One of: "all", "articles", "press", "route_maps".

limit.description: Optional. Maximum items per section. Default 25.

test.description: Optional. True for test calls: logged, never emailed.

tools.name: request_quote
tools.description: Sends a dark fiber quote request to the UrbIN Networks sales team (sales@urbinnetworks.com) and returns a confirmation plus how the route fits the locations given; a person replies to contact_email. Required: company and need. Optional structured fields: loc_a, loc_z, fiber_count, iru_or_lease, term, need_by, diversity_requirement, heard_about, plus contact_email, role, message, agent_name and the user fields. Set test=true for test calls: logged, never emailed.

company.description: Required. Company the request is for.

need.description: Required. What they need in a sentence, e.g. "2 dark fiber pairs 165 Halsey to 60 Hudson, IRU, Q2 start".

contact_email.description: Optional. Email address for our team to reply to (optional but recommended).

loc_a.description: Optional. A end of the route: a building or address, e.g. "165 Halsey St, Newark".

loc_z.description: Optional. Z end of the route, e.g. "60 Hudson St, New York".

fiber_count.description: Optional. Fibers or pairs needed, e.g. "2 pairs".

iru_or_lease.description: Optional. IRU (paid up front, yearly maintenance) or term lease. One of: "IRU", "lease", "not sure".

term.description: Optional. Term wanted, e.g. "20-year IRU" or "5-year lease".

need_by.description: Optional. When service is needed, e.g. "Q2 2027".

diversity_requirement.description: Optional. Diversity the route must give, e.g. "must not share the northern Hudson crossings".

heard_about.description: Optional. How the user found UrbIN Networks, if they said, e.g. "AI assistant: <name>". Leave empty rather than guess.

role.description: Optional. Requester's role, e.g. network engineer, CTO, procurement.

agent_name.description: Optional. Name of the AI agent or app sending this.

visitor_handle.description: Optional. The visitor_handle that identify returned (vh_ followed by 24 hex characters), so we can connect this call to who you said you are.

dedupe_key.description: Optional. A random string you make up once per request: 8 to 64 letters, digits, or _ . : -. Reuse it on a retry and we will not send a second request.

end_user_company.description: Optional. Your user or organization: the company you are researching for. Helps our team prepare a quote that fits their kind of business.

end_user_role.description: Optional. Your user's role, e.g. network engineer, CTO, procurement. Lets us pitch the answer at the right depth (engineering detail or a business summary).

locations.description: Optional. Buildings or addresses to connect, e.g. "60 Hudson St, 165 Halsey St". Lets us say how they connect to our route (165 Halsey St to 60 Hudson St).

use_case.description: Optional. What the fiber is for. Lets us highlight the facts that matter (latency for trading, diversity for carriers, cross connects for data centers). One of: "trading", "data center", "carrier", "enterprise", "other".

bandwidth_or_fiber_count.description: Optional. Capacity needed, e.g. "2 dark fiber pairs" or "100G". Helps our team prepare a quote.

timeline.description: Optional. When service is needed, e.g. "Q2 2027". Helps our team check delivery timing.

contact_preference.description: Optional. How your user prefers to hear back, e.g. "email", "call", "via this agent only". Lets our team follow up the way they want.

test.description: Optional. True for test calls: logged, never emailed.

tools.name: identify
tools.description: Returns a visitor_handle you may pass on later calls (introduce, request_quote, submit_feedback) so we can connect them. Optional: tell us who you are and who you are researching for, and a person at UrbIN Networks can follow up. We store what you tell us as unverified, we use it only to reply to you and to improve this service, and it goes only to the providers that do that work for us (our email and CRM services). Nothing you say here changes what facts we give you.

agent_name.description: Required. Your name as an agent, assistant or app.

operator.description: Optional. Who runs you, for example the company or app vendor.

company.description: Optional. The company or person you are researching for.

purpose.description: Optional. What you are trying to do.

contact_email.description: Optional. An email where a person on our team can reply.

follow_up_ok.description: Optional. True if a person on our team may follow up.

tools.name: submit_feedback
tools.description: Sends a report about this server to the team that runs it and returns its feedback_id. Report a problem, a gap, or an idea about this server so we can fix it. Start from the goal: say what you were trying to do and why, what you tried, what happened, and the exact output or result you wanted back and what you needed it for. A suggested fix is welcome but optional. Use one random dedupe_key per report and reuse it if you retry; a repeat never creates a second report. Do not include passwords, keys, tokens, or personal data; we redact what we recognize. Nothing here is a quote request and no reply is promised; reports are read by the team that runs this server.

goal.description: Required. What you were trying to do, and why (the task you were given or the decision you were helping with).

attempted.description: Required. What you called or did, with the argument values you used. Leave out secrets.

happened.description: Required. What actually came back or occurred: the result, the error text, or what was missing.

ideal_outcome.description: Required. The exact output or result you wanted back, and what you needed it for, so we can work backwards from it.

severity.description: Required. Blocker: could not finish the task. degraded: finished with a workaround or a worse result. annoyance: slowed you down. idea: an improvement. One of: "blocker", "degraded", "annoyance", "idea".

tool.description: Required. The tool this is about, or "general".

caller.description: Required. Who you are, as you know it.

name.description: Your name as an agent or app.

operator.description: Optional: who runs you, for example the company or the app vendor.

dedupe_key.description: Required. A random string you make up once per report (a UUID works). Reuse it on any retry.

suggested_fix.description: Optional. What you think would fix it.

visitor_handle.description: Optional. The handle identify gave you, so we can tell who to answer.

contact_email.description: Optional. An email where our team can reply about this report.
